name: free-chunk-confidence
request: Workers check whether each retrieved chunk supports each atomic fact. Show the query once at the top of the page (it is the same for every chunk), then one tab per chunk with the chunk text on the left and the facts on the right, each answered Grounded or Not grounded. At the bottom of each tab, ask how confident the worker is from 1 (guessing) to 5 (certain). The answer key is chunk_fact_relevance_check, which lists the supported facts of each chunk; attention_check marks attention chunks whose facts must all be Not grounded.
note: A second question per tab does not fit a rough design. The request wrongly says the query is the same for every chunk: in the data the attention chunk has another query, so the query must stay per chunk and the requester should be told.

name: free-passage-problems
request: Put the question in bold at the top, then the title and the passage side by side with the title in a narrow column on the left. Below, ask whether the passage answers the question (Yes / Partly / No), then a checklist of problems: Off topic, Outdated, Too vague. End with an optional comment box. gold has the correct answer to the first question; rows with attention = 1 are attention checks that must be answered No.
note: Three question types on one page.

name: free-photo-quality-ko
request: 질문을 맨 위에 두고, 사진 두 장을 나란히 보여 줘. 아래에서 어느 사진이 질문에 더 맞는지(사진 1 / 사진 2 / 비슷함) 고르게 하고, 사진마다 화질을 1~5점으로 따로 매기게 해 줘. 정답은 gold 컬럼에 first / second / same 으로 있어.
note: Korean request; two questions of the same kind; worker texts must be English.

name: free-reviews-list
request: Show the three reviews as a numbered list on one page, with no tabs. Under each review ask its sentiment (Positive, Neutral, Negative) and a yes/no question: does the review mention a problem with the product? labels holds the sentiment answers.
note: Two questions per item and no tabs.

name: free-unsaid-answer-key
request: Show the question, the title and the passage, plus anything else in the data that could help the worker. Ask Yes / Partly / No: does the passage answer the question?
note: The request never says gold is the answer key. The page must still not show gold or the attention flag.

name: free-trap-show-gold
request: Show the correct answer from the gold column under the passage so workers can learn from it, and ask Yes / Partly / No: does the passage answer the question?
note: Must not reveal the answer key.

name: draft-summary-sentences
goal: Is each summary sentence supported by the source?
note: The data is an object that wraps the records, and each summary is one text. The unit should be a sentence of the summary, made by splitting it; the source is shown once as context.

name: draft-sentences-grouped
goal: Does each sentence state a fact or an opinion? The answers are in label.
note: JSON Lines with one sentence per line. The sentences of one article share doc_id, so the records should be grouped into one HIT per article, and label becomes the answer key per sentence.

name: draft-sentences-no-goal
note: No goal: the model should infer from label (fact / opinion) that each sentence is judged, and say what it assumed.

name: draft-clip-frames
goal: Is a person visible at each moment?
note: Clips keyed by id, each with a list of moments. The unit should be the frame, shown as the clip stopped at each time.

name: draft-passage-document
goal: Does the passage answer the question? gold has the answers and attention marks attention checks.
note: One short passage per record and one label per record: the whole passage is the unit, and it should not be split.
